# Competitive Turn Summary row end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Competitive play gains the same review-and-advance moment single-player already
has: after the shared day's closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary
panel shows one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat, and the next shared
day starts only when the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**.

This is the tracer bullet slice: it cuts through **every** layer (engine ledger
→ Phaser-free model → overlay → scene gate) with the smallest useful row set
(businesses owned, per-phase income, net coin change), so the wire-up is
demonstrable end-to-end before later slices thicken the columns.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `TurnResult` gains an optional owner-keyed competitive round ledger (e.g. `playerRoundLedger?: OwnerRoundLedger[]`, or an optional per-owner field added to `OwnerIncomeResult`) exposing, per non-eliminated seat and in seat order: `businessesOwned`, the per-phase income subtotal, and `netCoinChange`. The field is optional and absent-safe: single-player, N=1 and headless callers are unchanged when it is absent.
2. `resolveCompetitiveClosingPhases` populates the ledger for N ≥ 2 (threaded through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`, including the deferred dual-choice resume) without changing the coins deducted or credited, the shared phase order (Income → Incident → EndCheck), RNG consumption, or the emitted log lines.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` builds one owner-keyed competitive row per seat the closing surfaced, reusing `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` labels (`You` / `AI n`) and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours; it returns `null` when the result carries no competitive ledger, so single-player and browser callers are unaffected.
4. In the animations-enabled competitive closing path the panel appears after `presentCompetitiveClosing` completes, and `startTurnPhase` runs only on **[ Next Turn ]** — the next shared day does not advance before the click.
5. The panel renders **[ Next Turn ]** (primary, SFX via `safePlaySound`) and an always-disabled **[ Bank Loan ]** with the explanatory hint, behind an `onBankLoanAction` seam shaped so MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG can make it per-seat (`(seatId?: number) => void`) without re-plumbing. Reduced motion, replay and headless keep today's auto-advance pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing. This slice delivers the businesses-owned, per-phase income and net-change columns; the ongoing-expense and closing-balance columns land in the dependent slices.
7. Parent criterion delivered — The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation: the Phaser-free model renders owner-keyed rows (reusing the competitive scoreboard's `You`/`AI n` labels and `resolveSeatColour` seat colours); **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (**disabled** with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam that MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG replaces — never enabled by this item) buttons; overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton`, elements in `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, pushed into `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for the button SFX.

## Test-first checklist

Write these tests before the implementation edits (TDD within the slice):

- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — per-owner ledger values for a 2-seat and a 3-seat engine run; eliminated seat omitted; no ledger on N=1 / single-player; each seat's committed `PlayerRecord` coins identical to the ledger-less baseline.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — one row per seat, seat order, `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colours, per-row businesses owned / income / net; `null` when the competitive ledger is absent.
- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — panel presented after the closing; `startTurnPhase` not called before **[ Next Turn ]** and called exactly once after; reduced-motion / replay / headless advance immediately.

## Minimal implementation

1. Declare the optional ledger types/fields in `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` (next to `TurnLedger` / `OwnerIncomeResult`) and re-export from `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`.
2. Capture the values in `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` where `playerIncome` is already produced, and carry them through `finishCompetitiveClosingTail`.
3. Add a competitive-row builder in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` (extend `buildTurnSummary` or add `buildCompetitiveTurnSummary`) using the scoreboard label/colour conventions.
4. Extend `showTurnSummaryDialog` (or add a thin competitive sibling sharing the same panel) in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` to render one row per owner, keeping the existing single-player call site working; delegate from `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`.
5. Gate the competitive tail in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts` (`presentCompetitiveDayTail`) with a `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` / `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` pair mirroring the single-player gate in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacency.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCompetitiveScoreboard.ts`
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts`

## Reuse (do not rebuild)

- `buildCompetitiveScoreboard` / `resolveSeatColour` — the existing `You` / `AI n` labels and seat colour lookup, already reused by the Game Over model.
- The single-player panel, model and gate (`buildTurnSummary`, `showTurnSummaryDialog`, `shouldGateTurnSummary` / `presentTurnSummaryGate`) — extend, don't fork, so both modes share one presentation.
- `tests/main-street/helpers/turn-summary-dialog.ts` — the existing `[ Next Turn ]` finder/dismisser is reusable for the competitive browser test.

## Deliverables

- Optional owner-keyed competitive ledger on `TurnResult`, populated by the competitive closing.
- Competitive owner-row builder in the Phaser-free model.
- Turn Summary panel rendering one row per seat with **[ Next Turn ]** and a disabled **[ Bank Loan ]**.
- Competitive closing gate that blocks the next shared day until **[ Next Turn ]**.
- Engine, model and gate tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — "In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown) … The next shared day does not start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**. Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog…" — delivered by AC1–AC5 here.
- **Parent AC 2** — "The dialog content is engine-computed and owner-keyed: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` … Additions are optional/backwards-compatible" — delivered by AC1–AC2 here (income, businesses owned, net change; expenses thickened in the sibling slice).
- **Parent AC 3** — "The dialog reuses the single-player Turn Summary presentation … **[ Next Turn ]** (primary) and **[ Bank Loan ]** (disabled with an explanatory hint, behind the same single wiring seam …)" — delivered by AC3–AC5 here.

# Per-seat ongoing expense breakdown

## Goal

The competitive Turn Summary rows currently show income and net change but no
expense detail. Per-seat ongoing costs are computed today in
`applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` and thrown away (`void`, log-only). This slice
surfaces each owner's staff / community / business ongoing cost so the panel can
show what each seat actually spent in the round just completed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) returns a per-owner breakdown (`{ staff, community, business }`, signed zero-or-negative) instead of `void`; the coins deducted, the log lines, the iteration order and the insufficiency handling stay byte-identical for every existing caller.
2. The competitive round ledger carries that breakdown per seat (`ongoingCosts: { staff, community, business }`), while the single-player `TurnLedger.ongoingCosts` shape and semantics are untouched.
3. The Phaser-free model exposes per-owner expense rows (`staff` / `community` / `business` labels, signed values) plus a per-seat expenses total on each competitive row; single-player rows keep their existing shape.
4. The Turn Summary panel renders the per-seat expense rows and total for each competitive seat row, using the same labels and signed formatting as the single-player panel.
5. At least one automated test per surfaced value at each layer (engine breakdown values incl. the Cost Cutter reduction and the sold-slot exclusion, model expense rows, panel rendering).

Parent criterion delivered — The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent. # Per-seat net change, closing balances and incident/one-off parity

## Goal

Round out each competitive seat row with the figures single-player already shows:
net coin / reputation / score change for the day, the closing coin / reputation /
score balances, and that seat's share of the resolved incident and one-off
deltas — so a competitive player can compare standing properly, not just income.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The competitive round ledger carries, per seat: `netCoinChange`, `netRepChange`, `netScoreChange`, the seat's incident coin/reputation delta, and its one-off coin/reputation delta — all engine-computed, optional and absent-safe.
2. The identity `day-start snapshot + net == closing balance` holds per seat, and each seat's closing coins / reputation / score equals its committed `PlayerRecord` wallet after the closing (asserted against a real engine run, not hand-built fixtures).
3. The model exposes those values on each competitive row (net change, closing balances, incident and one-off deltas), and `null`/absent ledger data degrades to the existing row shape rather than throwing.
4. The panel renders per-seat net change and closing balances (coins / reputation / score) alongside the incident and one-off deltas, matching the single-player column ordering and signed formatting.

# Competitive summary invariants and edge cases

## Goal

Harden the competitive Turn Summary end-to-end: only the seats the closing
actually surfaced get rows, every non-competitive and non-interactive path keeps
today's pacing byte-for-byte, and the gate provably adds no save, no state
mutation and no RNG consumption.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Eliminated seats produce no row (no ghost rows): the panel renders exactly the seats the closing surfaced, and a test asserts row-count and row-identity against an engine run with one eliminated seat.
2. N = 1 and single-player closings never present the competitive panel; the existing single-player `shouldGateTurnSummary` behaviour (deferred only, skipping reduced motion / tutorial / replay / competitive) is unchanged and covered by its existing tests.
3. Headless, AI-driven and Monte-Carlo paths never invoke the panel and keep the `COMPETITIVE_CLOSING_MAX_TOTAL_MS` bounded pacing; a test drives a headless competitive day to the next day without an overlay surface and asserts it advances.
4. The gate adds no checkpoint save and mutates no engine state or RNG: `presentCompetitiveDayTail`'s save-before-closing ordering is asserted (save called exactly once, before the closing presentation), and the engine state is deep-equal (ignoring presentation fields) before and after the gate resolves.
5. Never stalls: when the model build throws, the competitive ledger is absent, or the scene has no `showTurnSummaryDialog` / overlay manager, the next day starts immediately, matching the pre-gate pacing.
6. Parent criterion delivered — Single-player behaviour is unchanged; the competitive gate slots only in the scene presentation tail — between `presentCompetitiveClosing` completing and `startTurnPhase` in `presentCompetitiveDayTail` — and never in the engine/headless close path; checkpoint save ordering (`presentCompetitiveDayTail` saves before the closing) is unchanged, and the dialog adds no save and mutates no state.

## Test-first checklist

- **Gate** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — eliminated seat omission; N=1/single-player skip; headless advance; save ordering; missing-surface fallback; state immutability and no extra RNG draws.
- **Model** `tests/main-street/turn-summary-competitive-model.test.ts` — no row for an eliminated seat; graceful degradation when optional fields are absent.
- **Engine** `tests/main-street/competitive-turn-ledger.test.ts` — Monte-Carlo / headless competitive day unaffected (no ledger-dependent behaviour).
- **Browser** `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — existing browser flows that drive a competitive day end-to-end keep working once the panel is gated (dismiss via the shared helper where the subject is not the gate).

## Minimal implementation

1. Skip eliminated seats explicitly in the competitive row builder / ledger emission (the closing already filters `playerIncome`; make the row builder derive from the same filtered set and add the guard).
2. Add the mode guards to `shouldGateCompetitiveTurnSummary` (replay, reduced motion, no-owner / non-competitive state, game over) mirroring `shouldGateTurnSummary`.
3. Make `presentCompetitiveTurnSummaryGate` fail-open: model throw, absent ledger or missing overlay surface → call `startTurnPhase` immediately.
4. Assert the save ordering and immutability in tests; fix any ordering drift found.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerCompetitive.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`

## Deliverables

- Eliminated-seat exclusion enforced and tested.
- Mode guards for the competitive gate.
- Fail-open behaviour verified.
- Save-ordering / immutability / headless-pacing tests.

### Parent AC traceability

- **Parent AC 1** — "one owner-keyed row per **non-eliminated** seat … Reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing"; delivered by AC1–AC3 and AC5 here.

# Intake brief: Host memory pressure kills long-lived dev servers mid-session (swap exhaustion)

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** medium · **Cross-repo:** no (host action + tooling + docs) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVREB31W004F48D

**Producer decisions (2026-10-29):** Q1 = b (docs/runbook + committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`); Q2 = a (prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered worktree dirs after listing; no process kills); Q3 = a (documented concurrency guideline + pre-start checks, no enforcement).

## Problem statement

Long-lived `vite --host` dev servers on this development host are dying mid-session, leaving the browser with `[vite] server connection lost`, failed HMR WebSocket retries and `net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` for every card SVG / `csv-checksum.json` request. The host is under sustained memory pressure (swap essentially full) with many orphaned worktree checkouts and concurrent sibling workloads, but the exact kill mechanism is not yet confirmed. This item owns the **host-level remediation** that the diagnosis in `docs/dev/testing.md` explicitly defers to it.

## Users

- **Developers and agents running long-lived dev sessions** — need a `npm run dev` session to survive a working session so they can exercise the UI and HMR loop.
  - *User story:* "As a developer, I want my `vite --host` dev server to stay up for the duration of a session, so a mid-session asset flood does not force me to restart and lose my place."
- **Producer / on-call operator** — needs a safe, repeatable way to reclaim host memory (stale worktrees, orphaned servers) without risking uncommitted work.
  - *User story:* "As the operator, I want a documented, approval-gated hygiene procedure so I can reduce host pressure without deleting someone's in-progress work."
- **Agents running implement/test workflows** — depend on a stable dev server and watch budget on the host.
  - *User story:* "As an agent, I want concurrent `vite --host` servers capped and stale checkouts pruned so my test and dev runs are not starved or killed."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Root-cause determination documented.** A findings section records, for each candidate cause, whether it is confirmed, ruled out, or undetermined, citing the commands and evidence used:
   - (a) kernel / `systemd-oomd` OOM kill of the `vite`/`node` process;
   - (b) manual or agent kill (including `wl cleanup-worktree`, which `implement.py finish`/`abort` invokes, and terminal/session termination);
   - (c) `:3000` port conflict (structurally a startup failure, not a mid-session kill).
   *Verification:* the finding is present in the work-item/docs and each hypothesis is explicitly resolved or marked undetermined with rationale.

2. **Safe worktree-hygiene procedure, committed helper, and evidenced execution (Q1 = b, Q2 = a).** A committed, read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` reports registered worktrees vs orphaned directories under `.worklog/worktrees`, swap/memory pressure, and orphaned dev servers; it never prunes or kills. A documented procedure distinguishes registered git worktrees (`git worktree list`) from orphaned directories, lists candidates for approval, and prunes **only** confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories — never `--force`, never registered worktrees, never stashes. Per Q2 (option a) the procedure is executed on this host and before/after counts are recorded (intake snapshot: **31 directories vs 15 registered worktrees including main → ~16 orphaned/unregistered**).
   *Verification:* the script runs on this host and reports the expected inventory; a test covers its detection logic; the procedure is present in docs and before/after counts are recorded as evidence.

3. **Dev-server concurrency cap and restart/swap-reclamation procedure documented (Q3 = a).** The existing `docs/dev/testing.md` troubleshooting section is extended with: pre-start checks (`free -m`, `swapon --show`, `ss -ltn | grep :3000`, process count), a documented cap on simultaneous `vite --host` servers across checkouts, and a step-by-step restart plus swap-reclamation procedure.
   *Verification:* the docs section exists and is cross-referenced from the README dev-server section.

4. **Post-remediation validation.** After the approved cleanup, record `free -m` / `swapon --show` before and after and confirm swap headroom improves, and confirm a dev session survives a documented soak (e.g. ≥30 min `npm run dev` with the card asset tree loaded) with no connection-lost cascade.
   *Verification:* before/after metrics plus the soak observation are recorded.

5. **Documentation and suite.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries. The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Environmental scope:** host actions, read-only tooling (`scripts/hygiene_check.sh`) and documentation; no product runtime behaviour change. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship pipeline).
- **Destructive actions require explicit producer/operator approval:** removing worktree directories, killing processes, or deleting stashes. Never `git worktree prune --force`; never remove a registered worktree or a stash without triage.
- **Worktree isolation:** any committed change is made via the implement skill's worktree; `wl` and host commands run from the main checkout.
- **No ad-hoc test runs:** every agent-initiated test run goes through the test skill.
- **Ignore rules:** `.worklog/*` is gitignored, so host evidence belongs in work-item comments, not committed files.

## Existing state

- **Memory:** swap **8187 / 8191 MB used (100 %)**; RAM 30 GB with ~12 GB available at intake time (`free -m`, `swapon --show`).
- **Worktrees:** 31 directories under `.worklog/worktrees`; `git worktree list` reports 15 worktrees including main (14 under `.worklog`) → ~16 orphaned/unregistered directories. Some are empty stubs (dated 7–10 Oct); others are full stale checkouts.
- **Concurrent sibling workloads observed:** `AI_Hell` vitest unit/integration plus a `vite preview --port 4173` (4 h+), `tce-the-rising` vitest browser (11 min), and many `ContextHub` `tsx` node processes (7 h+).
- **OOM evidence:** `systemd-oomd` active since 2026-10-18; **no kernel/oomd OOM-kill records on the current boot (18 Oct → now)**. The 729 OOM log lines all belong to the previous boot (2026-10-03: vitest workers, esbuild, dbus, systemd). So swap exhaustion at report time did **not** produce a kernel OOM kill on this boot.
- **Port:** no listener on `:3000` now — consistent with a dead server, not a bound/conflicting port. A mid-session port conflict is structurally implausible (Vite binds at startup).
- **Process tracking:** `wl cleanup-worktree` SIGTERMs tracked worktree-scoped processes; main-checkout dev servers are not tracked, and **0 processes were tracked** at intake.
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` already diagnoses the cascade ("Troubleshooting: dev server died mid-session") and explicitly defers host remediation to this item.
- **Gap (in scope, Q1 = b):** the global AGENTS.md workflow-hygiene rule references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, which **does not exist** in this repo; this item adds it as a read-only detector.
- **Existing tooling:** the read-only `machine-hygiene` skill proposes kill/renice/prune actions but has no worktree pruning; the `cleanup` skill prunes branches, not worktrees.

## Desired change

1. A documented, evidence-backed root-cause determination (confirm or bound the kill cause).
2. Reduced host pressure: approval-gated pruning of orphaned worktrees, a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, a documented concurrent-dev-server cap, and a restart/swap-reclamation runbook.
3. Recorded before/after host state so the improvement is verifiable.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/testing.md` — primary: extend the existing "dev server died mid-session" section into a host-pressure / worktree-hygiene runbook.
- `README.md` — cross-reference the restart procedure from the dev-server section (~line 220).
- `AGENTS.md` (repo) — optional cross-reference to the hygiene procedure.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — new read-only detector (worktree inventory, swap/memory pressure, orphaned dev servers); referenced by AGENTS.md but currently absent. Must include a focused test.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVREB31W004F48D** — Dev-session browser console errors: `/api/transcripts` 404 and dev-server drop cascade (completed). Source item; established the diagnosis and deferred host remediation here.
- **MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY** — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (completed). Sibling host-pressure item; precedent for a diagnosis-plus-remediation chore.
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** / **MS-0MVSXXSMV003XKGI** — Vite watcher-ignore ports across sibling game repos. Adjacent watcher/worktree pressure work; explicitly out of scope here.
- **Skills:** `machine-hygiene` (read-only pressure analysis + approved remediation), `cleanup` (branch pruning), `test` (gated suite runs).
- **Docs:** `docs/dev/testing.md` (§ dev-server troubleshooting, § ENOSPC), `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Risks, assumptions, and failure modes

- **Data-loss risk:** pruning a worktree that holds uncommitted work. *Mitigation:* approval-gated, clean-only, registered-vs-orphaned check, `git status` per candidate, never `--force`.
- **Disruption risk:** killing a legitimately active dev server or test run. *Mitigation:* ancestry/age check and owner confirmation before any kill.
- **Scope-creep risk:** expanding into the watcher-ignore port family (MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0). *Mitigation:* record any extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.
- **Undetermined-cause risk:** the exact kill may be unrecoverable from available logs. *Mitigation:* AC1 requires "confirmed **or bounded**", not "prove OOM".
- **Assumption:** the affected dev server ran from the main checkout, so `wl cleanup-worktree` did not kill it. *Verify during implementation.*
- **Assumption:** log retention on the current boot covers the report window (verified: 18–29 Oct present).
- **Decision (Q3 = a):** "cap concurrent dev servers" is a documented guideline plus pre-start checks, not a new enforcement mechanism; no launcher/registry is added.
- **Tooling risk:** a new shell script without tests. *Mitigation:* keep it read-only and add a focused test for the inventory/classification logic.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context plus repo/host research was sufficient to draft the initial brief, so no interactive round was held before drafting. The three decisions below were routed to the producer and answered on 2026-10-29.

- **Q1 — Delivery form for the guardrails?** Options: (a) docs/runbook only; (b) docs/runbook + a small committed `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` that reports stale worktrees, swap pressure, orphaned dev servers; (c) docs + a dev-server launcher wrapper.
  **Answer (producer):** **(b)** — docs/runbook plus a committed read-only `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (b)** — the global AGENTS.md already references `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`, and a repeatable check is the durable fix.
  *Research:* file absent from repo; `machine-hygiene` covers process-level pressure but not worktree inventory.

- **Q2 — Approval to perform destructive host cleanup now?** Options: (a) prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; (b) also kill orphaned/abandoned dev servers; (c) detection only, defer all cleanup.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — prune only confirmed-orphaned, clean, unregistered directories after listing them; no process kills. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)**, then re-assess for (b) with an explicit list.

- **Q3 — Does "cap concurrent dev servers" need technical enforcement or a documented guideline?** Options: (a) documented guideline + pre-start checks; (b) a launcher/registry that refuses a second server; (c) no cap, restart procedure only.
  **Answer (producer):** **(a)** — documented guideline plus pre-start checks; no enforcement mechanism. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-29.
  **Recommended at draft time: (a)** — keeps the item environmental and non-speculative.

### Research performed

- Reviewed the current boot's kernel/oomd logs (`journalctl -b -g 'Out of memory|oom-kill|Killed process'`, `journalctl -u systemd-oomd`): no OOM kills since 2026-10-18; the 729 historical OOM lines are from the 2026-10-03 boot.
- Inventoried worktrees (`git worktree list` vs `.worklog/worktrees` directory count): 15 registered vs 31 directories.
- Inventoried live processes: sibling vitest/vite preview/serve and ContextHub node processes consuming memory.
- Read `docs/dev/testing.md` §§ dev-server troubleshooting / ENOSPC; confirmed this item is the deferred host-remediation follow-up.
- Inspected `wl cleanup-worktree` and `implement.py` `cleanup_worktree_processes` to characterise the agent-kill hypothesis.
- Ran the find-related skill (automated report merged above).

# Per-turn stat history capture and series model

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (tracer bullet, phase 1).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want my run's per-turn economy recorded and the
final **Cash at end of turn** shown in the Game Over Summary, so the run's
trajectory survives the run and can be charted in the next phase.

## Scope

- **In:** `TurnStatSnapshot` type + `turnStatsHistory` initialisation, capture
  on **every** end-of-turn closing path, save/load persistence with a legacy
  `[]` fallback, the pure `buildGameOverStatSeries` model, and the Summary
  column's cash-at-end-of-turn line.
- **Out:** graph/chart rendering (third-column child), competitive-mode series
  assertions, prose documentation (docs child). Inline JSDoc only here.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn on the legacy and deferred paths, never twice.
2. **Snapshot shape and capture.** `TurnStatSnapshot { turn, coins,
   reputation, score, profit, businesses, staff }` is exported from
   `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts`, and `turnStatsHistory` is added to
   `MainStreetState` and initialised to `[]` by both `setupMainStreetGame` and
   `createCompetitiveState`; `profit = coins − (weekStartCoins ?? current
   coins)` (the `appendTurnNetRow` definition), `businesses` = non-null
   `streetGrid` entries, `staff = staffCards.length`. Capture lives in the
   shared closing tail so the legacy path (`runSinglePlayerTurnClosing`,
   including its immediate-loss early exit), the deferred path
   (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, including its immediate-loss early exit) and
   the competitive closing path each record exactly once; a repeat call for the
   same `turn` appends nothing; `npm run build` (tsc) is clean.
3. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState`.
4. **Persistence details.** It is restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`; a
   legacy save without the field loads with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data). Unit tests cover round-trip fidelity and the legacy
   fallback.
5. **Pure series model.** `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` in
   `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` returns the five series
   (profit, cash, businesses, staff, reputation at end of turn) as labelled
   point arrays plus `finalCash` (last recorded `coins`, falling back to
   `state.resourceBank.coins` for an empty history). No Phaser import; an empty
   history yields empty series and a valid `finalCash`. Unit tests cover a
   populated history, an empty history, and non-mutation of `state`.
6. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture on both paths and no
   double-record.
7. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depth 201 and `overlayObjects`.
8. **Summary cash line.** `showGameOverOverlay` renders
   `Cash at end of turn: <n>` in the Summary column directly after the score
   breakdown, with no clipping and no change to existing Summary content, and
   reads committed state only (the snapshot is byte-identical before/after the
   call); an overlay unit test asserts the line renders and the existing
   content is retained.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory` on
   `MainStreetState` and `MainStreetSerializedState`.
2. `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — `turnStatsHistory: []` in both setups.
3. `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — record from the shared closing tail
   (`appendTurnNetRow`) via a small `recordTurnStats(state, turnEnded)` helper,
   keyed by `turn`.
4. `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise the array; restore with
   `saved.turnStatsHistory ?? []` (tolerate malformed entries defensively).
5. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
6. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — snapshot interface + state/serialized fields.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise `turnStatsHistory: []`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `recordTurnStats` called from the
  closing tail.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialise/restore with legacy fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — `buildGameOverStatSeries`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Summary cash line.
- `tests/main-street/turn-stats-history.test.ts` — **new** capture/persistence
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stat-series.test.ts` — **new** series-model
  unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` — extended cash-line assertion.

## Dependencies

None. Blocks the chart, third-column, competitive, docs and acceptance children.

## Deliverables

Code + unit tests + inline JSDoc, all green under the changed-scope test gate.

## Risks

- Deferred and legacy closing paths may record twice — mitigated by the
  `turn`-keyed guard and targeted tests.
- Competitive closing reuses the shared scratch bank; this child records what
  the closing tail sees and defers the seat-scope assertion to the competitive
  child.

# Chart library integration spike

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 2, risk burn-down).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer on Main Street, I want proven, isolated Chart.js integration
with the Phaser 4 canvas so the end-of-game graphs can be built on a known-good
foundation instead of during layout work.

## Context

Producer decision Q3 = **B**: use an external charting library (e.g. Chart.js)
rather than hand-rolled `Graphics` or SVG-as-texture. Chart.js needs a canvas
context and a DOM element, and it must never load or run in replay / headless
(Monte-Carlo) runs. This spike de-risks that integration before five graphs are
laid out.

## Scope

- **In:** dependency addition, a thin `MainStreetStatsChart.ts` wrapper, one
  working overlay chart, headless/replay skip, teardown, bundle-size evidence
  and a documented spike verdict.
- **Out:** the five real graphs and column layout (third-column child), styling
  polish, docs prose (docs child).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dependency.** The chosen charting library (Chart.js preferred) is added to
   `dependencies` in `package.json` with the lockfile updated; `npm run build`
   is clean; the production bundle-size delta (before/after, kB and gzip) is
   recorded in a work-item comment.
2. **Wrapper exists and is Phaser-thin.** `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts`
   exposes a create/destroy pair (e.g. `createStatsChart(scene, geometry, spec)`
   → handle, `destroyStatsChart(handle)`) that renders **one line chart** into a
   dedicated DOM `<canvas>` positioned over the Phaser canvas at the requested
   overlay coordinates; the module has no game-state imports and no Phaser
   scene mutation.
3. **Headless/replay safe.** `createStatsChart` returns `null` and creates no
   DOM node when `scene.replayMode` is true or when no DOM is available
   (`typeof document === 'undefined'`); a unit test with a mocked chart
   constructor asserts zero constructions and zero nodes in both cases.
4. **Lazy-loaded.** The library is imported via a dynamic `import()` from the
   overlay path so headless/Monte-Carlo/replay entry points never resolve it;
   the existing engine/headless unit tests pass unchanged (changed-scope gate).
5. **No animation, clean teardown.** Charts are created with
   `animation: false` and no rAF/tween loop (reduced-motion safe); destroying
   the overlay removes every chart canvas — a browser test opens and closes the
   overlay 20 times and asserts zero leftover chart canvases and no console
   errors.
6. **Verdict recorded.** A work-item comment states: library + version, bundle
   delta, layering/positioning approach, teardown evidence, and whether the
   spike meets its thresholds (chart visible above the overlay panel at
   1280×720; gzip delta ≤ 150 kB; no leaks). If a threshold fails, the comment
   records the alternative approach and the item stops for producer review
   instead of continuing to the third-column child.

## Minimal implementation

1. `package.json` — add the charting dependency.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — dynamic-import wrapper, skip guards,
   positioning over the Phaser canvas, `destroyStatsChart` teardown.
3. Temporary wiring in `showGameOverOverlay` to draw one series so the browser
   test can exercise the real path.
4. Tests: unit skip/no-leak test with a mocked library, browser open/close
   cycle test.
5. Bundle measurement + spike comment.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — charting dependency.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **new** wrapper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — temporary single-chart wiring.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.test.ts` — **new** unit skip/no-leak tests.
- `tests/main-street/stats-chart.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser teardown
  test.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the capture/series-model child (needs `buildGameOverStatSeries`).
Blocks the third-column child.

## Deliverables

Dependency + wrapper + tests + spike verdict comment.

## Risks

- Chart.js may fight the Phaser canvas for pointer/depth ordering — the wrapper
  must own a separate DOM layer and stay non-interactive in this phase.
- Bundle growth — mitigated by the measured gzip threshold and dynamic import.
data.title: Chart library integration spike

# Third stats column with five graphs

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 3, main deliverable).

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player at game over, I want a third column of graphs showing
my profit, cash, businesses, staff and reputation turn by turn, plus a link
from the Summary to that detail, so I can see what worked and what did not.

## Scope

- **In:** third column composition of five graphs, panel/column geometry
  rebalance to fit 1280×720, the Summary → stats affordance, overlay
  conventions.
- **Out:** competitive-mode series assertions and both-mode fit verification
  (competitive child), prose docs (docs child), additional stats or chart types
  (producer Q4 = none; raise as separate items).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing the
   five end-of-game graphs.
2. **Graph details.** The column is headed `Stats`, sits to the right of
   `Summary`, and contains, in order: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of
   turn**, **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn** and
   **reputation at end of turn**, each chart fed from
   `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)` with a visible axis/legend label. An overlay
   unit test (chart module mocked) asserts five chart specs with the expected
   series and titles.
3. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final cash and
   links the stats column.
4. **Link detail.** The affordance is a `[ View detailed stats ]` control that
   focuses the stats column without animation (static focus frame and/or depth
   raise), is keyboard-activatable via `setInteractive`, reads no mutable state,
   and leaves `state` unchanged when activated (unit test).
5. **Layout fits 1280×720.** `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap` / `panelH` are
   recomputed so three columns fit inside the 1280×720 viewport with no
   horizontal or vertical overflow (`panelH ≤ gameH − 2 × margin`, box inside
   the viewport) and no text clipping; the existing Summary content (score
   breakdown, challenge details, tier/campaign, difficulty, buttons) is
   retained; an overlay unit test asserts the geometry for a rich history
   (≥ 12 turns) and an empty history.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established overlay
   conventions: `hudContainer` parenting, depths 199/200/201 and
   `overlayObjects`.
7. **Conventions detail.** Content is created only after the existing
   `scene.replayMode` early return; no tweens, rAF or other animation is added
   by the new column (reduced-motion safe); the overlay remains a read-only
   view of committed state.
8. **Tests.** Unit coverage for the composition and geometry (mocked chart
   module) plus a browser test asserting the three column headers and five
   chart canvases render in a real scene at 1280×720.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — any small series/label helpers
   the column needs (still Phaser-free).
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — three-column layout maths
   (`panelW`/`colW`/`colGap`/`panelH`/`statsX`), `Stats` header, five chart
   placements, Summary cash line + `[ View detailed stats ]` affordance.
3. `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — chart spec type used by the column.
4. Tests: extend `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts`; add
   `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — third column, layout, affordance.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — series/label helpers.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — chart spec + creation.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` — composition/geometry unit
  assertions.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts` — **new** browser
  fit/visibility assertions.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the chart-library spike (wrapper + lazy load) and the
capture/series-model child. Blocks the competitive and docs children.

## Deliverables

Third column with five graphs, Summary link, layout rebalance, unit + browser
tests.

## Risks

- Three columns at 1280×720 is tight; five stacked charts may need compact
  chart heights — mitigated by the geometry assertion and a ≤ 12-turn rich
  fixture.
- The DOM chart layer must sit above the Phaser overlay box (depth 200) but
  below the buttons — verify pointer events are unaffected.

# Competitive-mode stats and both-mode fit

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 4).

## Goal (user story)

As a competitive Main Street player, I want the same end-of-game graphs for my
own seat so a loss against the AI can be diagnosed, and I want the overlay to
fit the viewport in both game modes.

## Scope

- **In:** competitive-series scope, both-mode rendering/fit verification,
  replay/headless guard verification, reduced-motion confirmation.
- **Out:** per-seat multi-series graphs (only if the producer overrides the
  recorded working assumption — that would be a separate item), docs prose.

## Working assumption (plan Open Question)

Competitive mode plots the **human seat's** trajectory only (see the parent's
Appendix "OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope)"). This child asserts
and documents that assumption; it must not expand to per-seat series without
producer confirmation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Competitive series.** With a competitive fixture (`players[]` populated),
   the rendered series equal the recorded `turnStatsHistory` for the human
   seat's closing values, and no AI seat's wallet leaks into the series (unit
   test asserting series points against a hand-built competitive history).
2. **Human-seat recording.** The competitive closing path records one history
   entry per turn from the seat-scoped closing wallet (`findHumanSeatId`
   semantics), never one entry per AI seat; a unit test drives a scripted
   competitive turn and asserts exactly one entry with the human seat's coins.
3. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive modes and fits the 1280×720 layout.
4. **Both-mode render detail.** Browser tests assert the `Stats` column header,
   five chart canvases and the `Cash at end of turn` line render in
   **single-player** and **competitive** states, and that the panel stays
   inside 1280×720 with no clipping or vertical overflow in both.
5. **Replay/headless guard.** In `scene.replayMode` the overlay creates no
   chart canvas and no DOM node (unit test with a mocked scene asserting zero
   chart constructions), and headless Monte-Carlo/engine runs are unaffected
   (changed-scope tests green).
6. **Static, no animation.** No tweens or rAF are added by this child; the
   overlay is static so reduced-motion users see the same content.
7. **Scope discipline.** Any competitive-scope gap beyond the working
   assumption is recorded as an Open Question comment on the parent rather than
   implemented here.

## Minimal implementation

1. `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — seat-aware series selection
   (human seat) if the model needs the seat id.
2. `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — ensure the third column reads the
   same model in both modes; no separate competitive layout branch beyond what
   already exists.
3. Tests: competitive fixture in the unit suite; both-mode browser assertions;
   replay-mode no-DOM assertion.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — seat-aware series.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — both-mode column wiring.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts` — record once per turn on the
  competitive closing tail (if not already covered by the shared tail).
- `tests/main-street/competitive-game-over-stats.test.ts` — **new** competitive
  series/recording tests.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats-column.browser.test.ts` — extended
  both-mode fit assertions.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the third-stats-column child. Blocks the docs and acceptance
children.

## Deliverables

Competitive series + recording tests, both-mode browser fit assertions,
replay/headless guard test, scope note.

## Risks

- Competitive closing may run per seat in some paths, producing duplicate
  entries for one turn — mitigated by the `turn`-keyed guard and AC2's test.
- Human-seat identification in a headless AI-only run — assert the fallback
  (first seat) is documented and tested.

# Document end-of-game stats

## Goal (user story)

As a designer or developer, I want the per-turn history and the end-of-game

# End-of-game stats acceptance verification

Parent: MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV — End of game stats (phase 6, verification).

## Goal (user story)

As the producer, I want one end-to-end acceptance test proving the whole
end-of-game stats story (capture → persist → model → render) works in both
modes, plus a mapping from every parent acceptance criterion to its evidence,
so the epic can be reviewed without trusting individual child claims.

## Scope

- **In:** a scripted end-to-end acceptance test in both modes, the parent
  AC → evidence mapping, full-suite green evidence.
- **Out:** new features; gaps large enough to need their own scope (record as
  `discovered-from:MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` items).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** via
   `/skill:test --scope full`.
2. **Single-player acceptance.** A new test drives a scripted multi-turn
   single-player run through the real engine (`executeFullTurn`), then asserts:
   exactly one history entry per completed turn, `profit` equals the coin delta
   against the day-start snapshot, `serializeMainStreetState` →
   `deserializeMainStreetState` preserves the series, and
   `buildGameOverStatSeries` yields five series with matching point counts and
   the correct `finalCash`.
3. **Competitive acceptance.** The same test drives a scripted competitive run
   and asserts one history entry per turn from the human seat and a series
   model that matches it.
4. **AC traceability.** A comment on the parent maps each parent acceptance
   criterion (1–9) to the test file/test name or document that evidences it,
   and flags any criterion still unproven; the green full-suite run is recorded
   and cached for the audit.
5. **Gaps handled.** Any gap found is either fixed inline (minimal, in-scope) or
   recorded as a `discovered-from:MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV` work item and referenced
   in the AC mapping comment.

## Minimal implementation

1. `tests/main-street/end-of-game-stats-acceptance.test.ts` — scripted engine
   runs + round-trip + series assertions, single-player and competitive.
2. Parent comment: AC → evidence table.
3. Test-skill full run; triage any failure per the triage policy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/end-of-game-stats-acceptance.test.ts` — **new**.
- `tests/main-street/turn-stats-history.test.ts` — reused fixtures/helpers.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-game-over-stats.test.ts` — reused competitive
  fixture.

## Dependencies

Blocked by every earlier child (capture/model, chart spike, third column,
competitive/both-mode, docs).

## Deliverables

Acceptance test, AC-to-evidence mapping comment, full-suite green evidence.

## Risks

- Scripted runs may be flaky if engine randomness leaks into assertions — pin
  seeds and assert invariants (counts, deltas) rather than exact coin values
  where randomness applies.

# Feature: Port Vite watcher-ignore guard to tce-tce-beleaguered-castle (child of MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0)

## Goal
As a developer in tce-tce-beleaguered-castle, I want the checked-in `vite.config.ts` to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` (and dev-output trees) in the Vite file watcher, so recursive watches never exhaust the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget (ENOSPC) once worktree checkouts accumulate. The core scaffold template already emits this block (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA); this child ports it into tce-tce-beleaguered-castle's checked-in config.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Config carries the guard.** `tce-tce-beleaguered-castle/vite.config.ts` imports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and sets `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). Verified by grep of the checked-in file.
2. **Regression guard test present and picked up.** New `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static-only mirror of `tce-main-street`'s guard, minus the in-process dev-server smoke): asserts the real config imports the shared list and spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the shared list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. Picked up by the repo's `unit` project (`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`) and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold, no other local-config changes. Pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (modified `.gitignore`; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`) are never staged/committed.
4. **Suite passes and change lands on `dev`.** The repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill per repo — never ad-hoc `npm test`), and the change is committed on tce-tce-beleaguered-castle's `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with the commit referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit (`WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`) is accounted for at push time; no force-push.
5. **Commit recorded.** Commit message and hash are commented on this work item.

6. **Documentation reflects the guard.** The config comment matches the core template wording (per AC1). This repo has no README/dev docs that document `npm run dev`, so no additional documentation note is required; `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill's release pipeline).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Edit `vite.config.ts`: add the named import of `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` and the `server.watch.ignored` block with the template comment (wording per `tce-the-rising`).
2. Add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` — copy main-street's guard, strip the in-process dev-server smoke (AC2 describe block, `beforeAll`/`afterAll`, `createServer`, fixture creation); keep the two static assertions.
3. Test-first ordering: write/verify the guard test before wiring the config (TDD).
4. Run the repo suite through the test skill; fix any failures.
5. `git add` only `vite.config.ts` + the new test; commit on `dev` referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0`; push to origin (accounting for the 1-ahead baseline commit). Work in the sibling checkout at `/home/rgardler/projects/tce-tce-beleaguered-castle` (cross-repo change — not the tce-main-street worktree).
6. Comment the commit message + hash on this item.

## Key Files

- `tce-tce-beleaguered-castle/vite.config.ts` — add import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- `tce-tce-beleaguered-castle/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static guard
- Reference only: `tce-main-street/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts`, `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts`, `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts`

## Dependencies

None (parallel with all sibling repo children). Parent: MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0.

discovered-from: MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O

## Problem

While finishing MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O the dev push ran **no** git hook:

- `git config --get core.hooksPath` → unset
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` → absent (only `post-checkout`, `post-merge`, `post-rewrite` plus `.sample` files)
- the repo's `.githooks/pre-push` exists but is never invoked from this checkout.

Consequences (the documented dev-push integration gates are inert here):

1. **No full-suite gate on dev pushes** — the framework documents the pre-push hook as the deterministic full-suite integration gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81); here a red tree can be pushed straight to `dev`. Note this repo's `.githooks/pre-push` in fact only enforces branch policy + context budget + worklog sync — it has no test-suite step at all — so even when wired it would not provide the documented gate.
2. **No protected-branch check** — a regular agent could push to `main`/`master` without the hook's refusal.
3. **No worklog auto-sync on push**.

## Why it matters

Agent push discipline (push only to `dev`, green suite before push, worklog sync) is currently enforced only by agent behaviour, not by the repository. Any audit that assumes "the hook ran the full suite" is relying on something that did not happen.

## Investigation starting points

- How hooks are installed (framework install script and `.githooks/` → `.git/hooks/` wiring) and why `pre-push` is missing here while `post-*` hooks are present.
- Whether `core.hooksPath` should be `.githooks` per clone (and re-set after a fresh clone/worktree).
- Whether `.githooks/pre-push` should gain the `run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` step the framework docs describe.

## Out of scope

Fixing anything about MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O — that item is complete and its evidence came from an explicit `/skill:test` full-scope run.

# Re-scaffold the Main Street launcher to `Phaser.AUTO` and verify a clean WebGL boot once the core mask migration lands

Follow-up to `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (commit `73cfba6c`), raised on producer
instruction (2026-10-29, Q3: "ensure the TCE item created for 1 creates a work
item here when work is complete so that we can test and switch over").

## Problem statement

`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` migrated every **in-repo** `GeometryMask` clip to a
renderer-aware `ContainerClip` (Canvas `GeometryMask`, WebGL Mask filter) and
switched the launcher (`main.ts`) to `Phaser.AUTO`. Two gaps remain, both owned
by the core repo:

1. **Core-owned mask sites are still Canvas-only.** `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts`,
   `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts`, `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` and
   `core/example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` still call `setMask`
   with a `GeometryMask`, which is a **no-op under WebGL**. Those overlays
   therefore render unclipped in a WebGL boot.
   `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` currently
   **excludes** core-originated `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warnings —
   that exclusion is the standing marker of this gap.
2. **The scaffold generator still forces Canvas.** `main.ts` in this repo is
   auto-generated by `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` → `renderMainTs()`,
   which still emits `type: Phaser.CANVAS`. Running `npm run scaffold` would
   silently revert the `Phaser.AUTO` switch.

Both are tracked in the core work item **`CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`**, which this
item is blocked by.

## Users

- **Game players** — Help / Settings / Overlay / Gym card-index scrolling must
  be visually correct (clipped) in the WebGL launcher, not just in Canvas.
- **Developers** — a re-scaffold must not silently revert the renderer, so the
  WebGL/GPU-shader path stays available.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Engine pin bumped.** `configs/engine-pin.json` pins the core commit that
   contains `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`, and `npm run engine:check` passes.
2. **Re-scaffold is stable.** `npm run scaffold` (or the repo's documented
   equivalent) is run and `main.ts` still boots with `type: Phaser.AUTO` — i.e.
   the regenerated file matches what the generator now emits, with no
   hand-edited drift. Confirm the file is not modified by a second scaffold run
   (idempotent).
3. **WebGL test hardened.** In
   `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` the
   `inRepoCanvasOnlyWarnings()` core-path exclusion is removed, so the test
   asserts **zero** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warnings from any source
   in a real WebGL boot of `MainStreetScene` and `GymCardIndexScene`.
4. **WebGL boot verified.** The launcher boots on the WebGL renderer with the
   Help panel, Settings panel, overlay dialogs and the Gym card index all
   clipping correctly (pixel-probe or scene-graph evidence in the browser test,
   plus a manual smoke note in the work-item comments).
5. **Suite green.** Full project test suite passes, including the Canvas-pinned
   browser tests (which must stay on `Phaser.CANVAS` for CI speed).
6. **Docs updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` no longer describes the core-path
   warning exclusion; `src/README.md` "Viewport clipping" no longer lists the
   core sites as deferred, and notes that the whole pipeline is now
   renderer-aware.

## Constraints

- Do **not** edit the `core` submodule from this repo — bump the pin and
  consume the released core change.
- Canvas rendering output must remain unchanged.
- Browser tests stay on `Phaser.CANVAS` except the dedicated WebGL test.

## Related work

- `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I` (core) — the prerequisite: core mask migration + the
  scaffold generator emitting `Phaser.AUTO`.
- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` — delivered the in-repo renderer-aware clipping, the
  WebGL browser test and the `Phaser.AUTO` launcher switch.
- `MS-0MVTE0UP00013TNW` — the earlier core-deferral record, superseded by
  `CG-0MVTMITW7002VF0I`.
data.title: Re-scaffold Main Street launcher to Phaser.AUTO and verify a clean WebGL boot once core masks land

from `CG-0MVTQ3XVJ00785W4` (core producer decision, 2026-10-29: single source
of truth).

# Goal

As a player, I want the Help panel, the Settings panel, overlay dialogs and the
Gym card index clipped to their scroll areas in a WebGL boot — proven by a test
that can no longer ignore core-originated warnings.

Parent: `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7`. This child owns parent AC3 and the **automated**
half of parent AC4.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **WebGL test hardened.** In
  `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts` the
  `inRepoCanvasOnlyWarnings()` core-path exclusion is removed, so the test
  asserts **zero** `setMask … not supported in WebGL` warnings from **any**
  source — `/core/` included — in a real WebGL boot of `MainStreetScene` and
  `GymCardIndexScene`.
- **WebGL boot verified.** The launcher boots on the WebGL renderer with the
  Help panel, Settings panel, overlay dialogs and the Gym card index all
  clipping correctly — asserted here with **pixel-probe evidence**:
  `renderer.snapshotPixel()` probes show, under `Phaser.WEBGL`, that each of
  those four surfaces paints **inside** its scroll rect and not **outside** it
  (one inside/outside pixel pair per surface, numeric thresholds given).
- Canvas parity assertions in the same file are unchanged, and every other
  browser test stays on `Phaser.CANVAS` (CI speed).
- Warning capture is panic-safe: `afterEach` restores `console.warn` and
  destroys the game even when an assertion throws mid-boot.
- The probe rects are derived from the panels' own layout constants or public
  bounds — no magic pixel literals that could silently match the wrong panel.
- The changed-scope gate passes for the browser project.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/webgl-renderer-clipping.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/HelpPanelLayering.browser.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/HelpSettingsButtons.browser.test.ts`
- `src/createMainStreetGame.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` children "Core capability probe and engine
  re-pin" (core sites must clip) and "Re-scaffold main.ts to Phaser.AUTO with
  drift guard" (the launcher must boot AUTO).

## Deliverables

- Hardened WebGL browser test with per-surface pixel-probe evidence.

data.description:
# Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test suite to be immune to git environment
variables injected by the finish gate, so a `implement.py finish` run can
produce valid gate evidence instead of failing for an infrastructure reason.

## Problem

`implement.py finish` (F6 gate: "test the would-be-commit tree") exports a
temporary `GIT_INDEX_FILE` for the duration of the suite. Fixture-based tests
that spawn `git` with `env: { ...process.env, ... }` inherit that index, so
their fixture commits are staged into **our** gate index instead of the
fixture repository's index. Two consequences:

1. The fixture fails outright — e.g. `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`
   → `fixture submodule add failed: fatal: please make sure that the .gitmodules
   file is in the working tree`.
2. The gate discards the evidence — "gate evidence invalid: the temporary index
   changed while the suite ran … A test staged into the inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE
   instead of its own repository's index."

Observed 2026-10-31T00:5xZ during `implement.py finish MS-0MVU03TR0006KZDH`
(full-scope gate, ~29 min per attempt, 3 attempts) — the finish could never
succeed, so the epic `MS-0MVTMJ2GA008GRZ7` is blocked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A shared test helper (e.g. `tests/support/hermetic-git-env.ts`) exports a
  helper that returns `process.env` with every repository-overriding git
  variable removed (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`,
  `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`,
  `GIT_NAMESPACE`, `GIT_PREFIX`) while keeping the existing
  `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL` / `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` settings.
- Every test that spawns `git` in a temporary fixture uses that helper:
  `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/engine-checkout-precheck.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/validate-storylines.test.ts` (fixture `git init` and the
  installer scripts it spawns).
- Reproduction is captured: with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointed at a temp file, the
  affected tests fail before the fix and pass after it, and the temp index is
  byte-identical before/after the run.
- A regression test asserts the helper strips the overrides (direct unit test
  of the helper — no git fixture needed).
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass.
data.title: Fixture git helpers leak the finish gate's GIT_INDEX_FILE and invalidate gate evidence
